plan.title: GO BP over-representation: AD lesional vs control DE genes
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks which GO biological processes are over-represented among genes that came out significant in the treated (AD lesional) vs control comparison. A DESeq2 results table (12000 genes) already exists from a 6 vs 6 unpaired design; no new differential expression model needs to be fit. Per the grounded procedure: (1) confirm sample structure via vst-blind PCA/heatmap on the existing counts, explicitly inspecting sample_01 (library size ~4x below median) rather than dropping it silently; (2) determine the significant gene list from the delivered DESeq2 results at padj<0.05, check its size against the ~50-gene floor for a hypergeometric test to have any power, and if the list is short, run a preranked GSEA on the full ranked list (by the DESeq2 Wald 'stat' column) as the primary or a fallback additional finding; (3) map gene symbols to Entrez IDs with org.Hs.eg.db, reporting the unmapped share; (4) run clusterProfiler enrichGO (ontology=BP) over-representation with the universe set to all 12000 tested genes, gene-set size window 15-500, then reduce redundant GO terms with rrvgo semantic similarity; (5) report the representative BP terms, full table, database/version, universe, size window, and the enrichment-method-dependence caveat. WikiPathways human and MSigDB GO-BP (C5) collections are available in the reference store as secondary/cross-check collections if desired, but the primary answer uses clusterProfiler's internal GO.db (via org.Hs.eg.db), which is installed and current, matching the grounded procedure's tool of record.
